proposal.summary: Preserve existing discovery and quotation guidance, clarify review scope, and add a memory preventing verification from discarding stronger evidence.

edits.title: Diagnose missing biographical fields before further research
edits.content: When structured extraction leaves a biographical field empty, review the stored source specifically for explicit evidence of that field. Distinguish source absence from extraction omission. Do not derive nationality or citizenship from birthplace, education, or workplace. If evidence is absent, retain the unresolved field and search for a source explicitly stating the requested attribute; fetch and verify that evidence before filling the cell. For affiliations, distinguish employment and secondary appointments from educational institutions, and preserve temporal qualifiers such as former or emeritus. Pass the task's field definitions, time frame, and chosen source scope to extraction and review calls. If the task leaves scope ambiguous, make the working interpretation explicit and consistent. Assess reviewer suggestions against that scope before expanding research; for announcement-listed affiliations, unrelated advisory appointments are not omissions. Apply this review to unresolved fields without repeating successful searches or downloads.

edits.title: Compare verification results before replacing supported cells
edits.content: A follow-up extraction using narrower evidence replaced a supported multi-valued nationality with a single country from another person's page navigation. Schema and quote-membership checks passed despite the loss; the original evidence had to be restored. Supply the existing cell and its supporting evidence to verification calls. Stage proposed replacements and compare their scope, completeness, source relevance, and temporal meaning before committing them. A source mentioning only one value does not disprove other supported values, and a failed corroborating fetch does not invalidate evidence already collected. Preserve supported values unless stronger evidence explicitly corrects them; investigate genuine conflicts rather than blindly replacing or unioning results.

additional_candidates.description: Carry field definitions and source scope into semantic review to prevent unrelated affiliation investigations.
Prevent follow-up extraction from replacing stronger, complete evidence with a narrower supported subset.
Repair noncontiguous PDF quotations using exact stored source slices.

decisions.reason: All 34 occurrences have legitimate empty-discovery explanations: signals 0–6 concern seven annual searches whose snippets contained no laureate names; signals 7–31 concern 25 nationality searches for already identified people; signals 32–33 concern two further verification searches. Results were inspected before recording, unlike the premature placeholders described in the existing memory. These searches still supplied useful sources. Entry 0 explicitly permits honest empty discoveries, so its usage outcome does not establish consistently bad guidance or justify an edit.

The Princeton request failed with HTTP 403 and was recovered through an already discovered alternative profile. The TAP request failed certificate verification; previously fetched MIT evidence remained available and was ultimately retained. Neither URL was repeatedly retried, and neither failure supports a persistent domain prohibition or transport workaround. The consequential evidence-replacement regression is handled separately.

Annual reviews proposed investigating unrelated advisory and outside appointments after receiving a broad completeness instruction. The coordinator clarified that the working scope was affiliations recorded in award announcements; the final scoped review passed. Updating the existing biographical-review skill preserves this successful procedure without hardcoding that interpretation for every task. Its recorded outcome is successful, so targeted clarification is warranted rather than deletion.

The follow-up nationality extraction omitted the existing MIT evidence and returned one country from another person's page navigation. The coordinator committed that narrower cell, reported no structural or quotation errors, then explicitly restored the stronger original evidence. Final citation checks passed after recovery, but they do not prevent this semantic loss. Existing entries cover missing fields and quotation repair, not replacement regressions, so a separate failure memory is justified.

An affiliation quotation failed membership because it reconstructed interleaved PDF text incorrectly. The coordinator located and copied a contiguous source slice, and final citation checks passed. Entry 1 already describes this exact failure, repair, and revalidation procedure. Its successful outcome provides no reason to revise or duplicate it.
